case_title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Shyam Bihari & Others
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that three individuals, who were police officers on patrol, fired at a scooter carrying the deceased, resulting in his death. The deceased was traveling with two witnesses on a separate scooter. The witnesses claimed that the police officers flashed a torch light at them, causing their scooter to skid, and then fired shots at them, which led to the deceased's death. The witnesses managed to escape and later reported the incident. The prosecution also relied on the presence of empty cartridges at the scene, which were matched to the rifles of the accused. However, the deceased's injuries were caused by a .12 bore weapon, which was not recovered from any of the accused. The trial court found the eyewitness accounts of the witnesses inconclusive and the testimony of one witness unreliable, leading to the acquittal of the accused. The High Court dismissed the appeal, noting that the prosecution failed to establish the identity of the accused as the perpetrators.
